extraction.title: Meet the peptideins
extraction.subtitle: The human genome encodes for a new category of molecule They may be useful targets for future drugs
extraction.summary: A new class of tiny protein‑like molecules called peptideins has been mapped in the human genome, expanding the ‘dark proteome’. Researchers led by Sebastiaan van Heesch suggest they could become drug targets, especially for cancer immunotherapy, but warn that many may be false positives pending better validation.

narratives.name: Peptideins as a new drug target class
narratives.thesis: The discovery and systematic naming of peptideins will open a previously hidden layer of the proteome, providing novel targets for immunotherapies and other drugs.

narratives.name: Methodological validation challenge
narratives.thesis: Current ribosome‑profiling and mass‑spectrometry methods may over‑report peptideins, requiring improved validation to separate functional molecules from artefacts.
